inline_comments.comment: The truthiness filter `.filter(([, v]) => v)` deviates from the project's own `buildNavigationUrl` helper (in `lib/url.ts`), which uses an explicit `.filter(([, v]) => v !== null && v !== undefined)`. Although `customQueryParams` values are typed as `string | undefined` (no `null`), a truthiness check silently drops empty-string values while the explicit check does not. Align with `buildNavigationUrl`'s guard and with the project-wide convention of using explicit null/undefined checks rather than truthiness for string-presence tests.

`tagsValue || null` should be `tagsValue ?? null`. `serializeTagsParam` returns `string | undefined` (never an empty string), so both behave identically at runtime, but `||` would silently coerce a hypothetical empty string to `null` rather than surfacing it. The project rule is to prefer `??` over `||` for default-value fallbacks to avoid masking falsy-but-valid values.

`filteredIndex[storyId]?.type === 'story'` treats any docs entry as "not passing" the filter even when it is present in `filteredIndex`. Consider the scenario: the user navigates to `?path=/docs/my-component&tags=some-tag` and the docs entry passes the filter (i.e., `filteredIndex['my-component']` exists with `type: 'docs'`). The check still evaluates to `false`, so the redirect fires and the user is bounced away from the page they explicitly requested. The guard should check for presence in `filteredIndex` regardless of entry type:

```typescript
const entryPassesFilter = !!(filteredIndex && filteredIndex[storyId]);
```
or at minimum:
```typescript
const entryPassesFilter =
  !!(filteredIndex &&
    (filteredIndex[storyId]?.type === 'story' ||
     filteredIndex[storyId]?.type === 'docs'));
```

general_comments.comment: The PR removes the migration path for localStorage-persisted tag filter state (`layout.includedTagFilters` / `layout.excludedTagFilters` / top-level `includedTagFilters`) without any MIGRATION.md entry. Users who have saved filter preferences in localStorage will silently lose them on upgrade — after refreshing, they will see the preset defaults rather than their previous selections. This is a user-visible behavior change that warrants a MIGRATION.md note, even if the migration path is intentionally dropped.

The new filter-aware initial story selection code path (the `hasActiveFilters && !stateHasSelection` block inside the `STORY_SPECIFIED` handler) and the updated `selectFirstStory` have no dedicated unit tests. The existing `tags.test.js` tests only the pure serialization/parse helpers. Consider adding tests that assert: (1) navigating to a docs page whose tag passes the active filter is not redirected, (2) navigating to a story that fails the filter redirects to the first matching story, (3) when no story passes the filter, `selectFirstStory` returns without navigating (verifying the intentional no-op), and (4) the redirect for a docs `firstFiltered` entry uses `docs` as the view-mode prefix.
